spans.s: Vṛka^1, a prince. § 232 (Svayaṃvarap.): I, 186, 6990 (came to the svayaṃvara of Draupadī).
Vṛka^2, a Pāṇḍava warrior. § 592 (Saṃśaptakavadhap.): VII, 21, 867 (Pāñcalyaḥ, only B., the verse missing in C.), 868, 870 (slain by Droṇa).
Vṛka^4, an ancient king. § 761 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 115, 5665 (among the kings who abstained from meat during the month of Kārttika).
Vṛka, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 578 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 51, 2106 (B. Śakaiḥ, in Duryodhana's army).
Vṛkaratha, brother of Karṇa. § 600 (Ghaṭotkacavadhap.): VII, 157, 6942 (bhrātā Karṇasya, pierced Bhīmasena).

Vṛkasthala, a village. § 556 (Sañjayayānap.): V, 31, 934 (among the five villages for which Yudhishṭhira asked Duryodhana).--§ 562 (Bhagavadyānap.): V, 72, 2595 (do.); 82, 2877 (do.); 84, 3012 (a station on Kṛshṇa's way from Upaplavya to Hāstinapura.); 85, 3037; 86, 3040; 89, 3102 (ºnivāsinaḥ).
Vṛkodara, pl. a class of demons. § 615u (Skanda): IX, 45, 2607 (ºnibhāḥ, sc. some of the warriors of Skanda).
Vṛkshavāsin, a Yaksha, § 269 (Vaiśravaṇasabhāv.): II, 10, 399 (in the palace of Kubera; C. has by error Vṛkshavāspaniketaś ca instead of ºvāsy Aniketaś ca, B.).
